verdict.tagline: Explore a vibrant alien world and build a thriving slime empire.
for_you_if: you like collecting and breeding cute creatures

cohorts.label: <2h refund window
cohorts.summary: Players encounter dangerous tar slimes that threaten their farm early on.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe encountering an evil slime type called tar that attacks or overruns their farm.

citations.review_text: theres an evil slime made of tarr that gored my slimes very graphic and gorey. 10/10
Press play. Run around and collect slimes. 35 minutes into the game my entire farm is overrun by tar slimes. Geeg. 10/10

single_points.text: One reviewer notes that the Tar can be turned off before starting a new game.

citation.review_text: Such a classic, I love the cute little slime designs and the art style in general. This is a staple game for cozy gameplay, and isn't stressful to play in the slightest unless you get overwhelmed from the Tar but that can be turned off before starting a new game. I also love the DLC to change the style of the slimes

single_points.text: One reviewer states that they kept falling through the ground and losing all their stuff.

citation.review_text: How did this get 98% positive reviews? 30 minutes and I kept falling through the ground and losing all my stuff, going through tens of hours of that sounds masochistic. Really seems like something they should have fixed BEFORE making a sequel.

cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: Players continue building their ranch and exploring new regions.

single_points.text: One reviewer says it is, mechanically, an FPS that focuses on the farming.

citation.review_text:
Slime Rancher is probably the first game my oldest got really attached to.  Extremely colorful and full of style while being approachable mechanically with plenty of room to grow.  It starts as a simple farming sim that has plenty of exploration and options to keep the friendly slimes entertaining.  Even picked up some merch because of how much we enjoyed our time together playing through, exploring, and learning the world.

It is, mechanically, an FPS that focuses on the farming.  A single-player experience that does have an ending but can be played forever if one desires.  Great for the kids with little restraints in their play.

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Long-term players master the ranching mechanics completely.

single_points.text: One reviewer says the drone system lets you kind of forget about your ranch when you get a lot of slimes.

citation.review_text: The very first video game experience I've ever had. I couldnt be happier to start with a game with a fantastic artstyle, fun designs, and great open world. I loved finding out how all the different largos look like. I also loved the drone system that let you kinda forget about your ranch when you get a lot of slimes. The story isnt anything remarkable but thats not the reason you really play. The slime rancher 2 story is slightly better I say but not anything great either. Fantastic childhood

single_points.text: One reviewer says the mid game grind involves managing plort market prices, running back and forth across long distances for food, and cleaning up chaotic crossbred slimes that turn into black tar monsters during sudden Tarr outbreaks.

citation.review_text:
A cozy first person farming sandbox where you explore a weird wilderness and vacuum up colorful gelatinous creatures or pieces of jelly -whatever you call them-.  

The bad part is the mid game grind and sudden Tarr outbreaks. Managing plort market prices, running back and forth across long distances for food, and cleaning up chaotic crossbred slimes that turn into black tar monsters gets tedious.  

The good part is the incredibly relaxing exploration loop and satisfying ranch management. Upgrading your vacpack, feeding hungry slimes, discovering ancient secret zones, and expanding your farm builds a surprisingly addictive gameplay loop.
  
A charming cozy sandbox that makes hoarding bouncy colorful creatures genuinely fun, you are just there to chill.
